title: Six Fallacies in Substituting Large Language Models for Human Participants

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical review and literature synthesis of representational biases stemming from WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) training data, evaluating how models fail to capture global cultural nuances and human heterogeneity.
Conceptual analysis of how static training datasets, knowledge cutoffs, and recency biases cause 'temporal flattening,' evaluating how historical diversity is filtered through contemporary norms.

Critical evaluation of 'identity essentialization' in role-play prompting, highlighting how instructing models to adopt specific demographic labels produces stereotyped, one-dimensional responses rather than capturing intersectional human realities.

Analysis of how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and fine-tuning introduce artifacts such as sycophancy, excessive neutrality, and high agreeableness, distorting the natural distribution of human judgments.
